title: How to distinguish chaos from integrability using OTOC
abstract: The decay of out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs) to a small residual value signals the scrambling of quantum information. This behavior is generic: it occurs in both chaotic and interacting integrable many-body systems, and therefore cannot by itself distinguish between them. In this paper we analytically study the late-time saturation value of a closely related observable, operator purity, and show that its scaling with system size robustly distinguishes chaotic from integrable systems. Our approach is based on the Mazur bound, which provides concrete scaling estimates and makes explicit why the locality of integrable charges matters. We support our findings with numerical simulations of one-dimensional spin chains.
summary: This paper presents a method to distinguish quantum chaos from integrability by analyzing the late-time saturation of operator purity. Using the Mazur bound, the authors show that integrable systems exhibit a linear growth in this observable with subsystem size, whereas chaotic systems are bounded by a function of the subsystem size ratio. The findings are supported by theoretical derivations and numerical simulations on spin chains.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop a robust diagnostic tool to distinguish between quantum many-body systems exhibiting chaotic dynamics versus those that are integrable.
main_result: The late-time saturation value of the operator purity (or related quantities) scales differently for the two classes: it grows at least linearly with subsystem size in integrable systems, while it is bounded by a function of the ratio of subsystem size to total size in chaotic systems.
method: The analysis utilizes the Mazur bound applied to operator purity, which is related to Out-of-Time-Ordered Correlators (OTOCs). The distinction is drawn by analyzing the scaling of this bound based on the presence of extensive quasi-local conserved charges.
model_or_system: The study is applied to general one-dimensional quantum many-body systems, with numerical support provided by spin chains such as the XYZ and Ising models.
key_observables: Operator Purity ($	ext{Tr}ho^2_{A_1A_2}$), Out-of-Time-Ordered Correlators (OTOCs), and the late-time saturation value of these quantities.
important_parameters: Subsystem size ($L_A$), total system size ($L$), and the ratio $r_A = L_A/L$. The analysis focuses on the infinite-time average.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system is at infinite temperature ($ho$ is maximally mixed) and relies on the locality and existence of conserved charges for the integrable case.
figures_summary: Figure 2 numerically compares the saturation behavior of the operator purity for three models (XYZ, XYZ+NN, Ising), showing distinct scaling trends consistent with chaotic versus integrable predictions.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the diagnostic tool (operator purity/OTOCs) and the theoretical framework (Mazur bound). It then derives distinct scaling bounds based on the presence of conserved charges, supports this with detailed mathematical analysis, and concludes with numerical simulations on spin chains to confirm the theoretical distinction.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, theoretically grounded diagnostic tool for characterizing quantum dynamics in complex many-body systems, which is crucial for understanding thermalization and quantum chaos in condensed matter settings.
